title: Odd and even
examples: Teacher, how do I know if a number is even?
Can you show me some pairs of objects?
What is the rule for odd numbers?

explain.say: Today we will learn about odd and even numbers. We will look at making pairs with objects.
If we have two things, we can make one perfect pair. If we have three things, we will have one left over.
Let us count these apples. One, two, three. We can make one pair and one apple is left over.
If we have four blocks, we can make two perfect pairs. There are no blocks left over.
Now let us look at the last digit of a number. If it ends in two, four, six, or eight, it is even.

faq.q: What does it mean to make pairs?
faq.a: Making pairs means grouping things into sets of two. You put two items together so they match up.
asks: How do I check for pairs?
What is a pair of things?

faq.q: Why is the last digit important?
faq.a: The last digit tells us if the number can be split into perfect twos. Even numbers always end with 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.
asks: What do the digits tell us?

faq.q: Is the number five odd or even?
faq.a: Five is an odd number. If you try to make pairs with five, you will have one left over.
asks: How do I tell if 5 is odd?

faq.a: Ten is an even number. You can make exactly five perfect pairs with ten items.
asks: Can you show me ten items in pairs?

faq.q: What is the smallest odd number?
faq.a: The smallest odd number is one. It cannot be made into a pair.
asks: What is the first odd number?
What is the smallest number that is odd?

facts: Even numbers can always be divided by two with nothing left over.
Odd numbers always have one left over when divided by two.
Even numbers always end with 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.
Odd numbers always end with 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9.

quiz.say: Which group of numbers is all even?
quiz.why: The correct answer has only numbers that end in 2, 8, and 0, which are all even.
